headline: Approved six new CTE programs at Lowell High School, a $20,000 donation to Daley School, and a $10,000 budget modification
summary: The Lowell School Committee approved minutes, permission to enter, and several reports of progress, including confirmation that six Lowell High School programs received Career Technical Education status. The Committee also approved a $20,000 donation to the Daley School, a $10,000 budget modification, acceptance and expenditure of FY27 grant awards, an MOA on substitute pay for paraprofessionals, and home education requests for five students.

Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
LOWELL SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 
, 2025 
 
 
 
 
 
Date: September 2, 2026 
Time: 6:30PM 
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, Lowell, MA 01852 
____________________________________________________________________________________ 
Members of the public can view the meeting via LTC.  Those wishing to speak about a specific agenda 
item must register in advance by emailing the Superintendent.  Please include the agenda item, as well 
as your phone number and email address so we can provide a Zoom link for access. The email address is 
skeo@lowell.k12.ma.us. If you do not have access to email, you may contact us at 978-674-4324. All 
requests must be submitted by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. 
 
 
1. SALUTE TO FLAG 
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
On a roll call at 6:31 p.m., members present were, namely: Ms. Delrossi, Mayor Gitschier, Mr. Lay, Ms. 
McFadden, Mr. Bahou and Mr. Conway. Ms. Martin was absent. 
 
3. MINUTES 
 
3.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Regularly Scheduled Lowell School Committee Meeting of 
August 19, 2026 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept and place on file the minutes of the Regularly Scheduled School 
Committee meeting that was held on August 19, 2026; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
4. PERMISSION TO ENTER 
 
4.1. Permission to Enter – September 2, 2026 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve the Permission to Enter; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
5. MEMORIALS 
 
5.1. Nicholas J. Laganas, Husband of Karen Laganas, Executive Secretary for the Finance Department 
 
5.2. David J. Gwiazda, Father of Jeffrey Gwiazda, Math Coordinator of K-12 for the Curriculum 
Department
(Page 2 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
6. MOTIONS 
 
6.1. By Dominik Lay]: Ask the Superintendent for a report on the condition of each school at the opening 
day. If any, what needs to be done and what has been done to ensure a smooth opening day. 
Superintendent Skinner stated that he was very pleased with how the first day of school went and 
believed it was a successful opening. 
Ms. Crocker-Roberge added that two cafeterias, which could not be fully cleaned because summer 
school ended late, will be cleaned this Friday. She agreed that it was a successful opening. 
Mr. Conway requested that the district begin testing the boilers now to avoid any issues when colder 
weather arrives. 
Superintendent Skinner explained that the boilers are often serviced during the summer, after which the 
Department of Public Works (DPW) must return to reassemble them. He said he would look into the 
matter. 
Mayor Gitschier stated that he would also check with the City Manager. 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 
absent (Ms. Martin).  
 
7. SUBCOMMITTEES 
 
7.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Human Resources & Labor Relations Subcommittee Meeting of 
August 26, 2026 
 
Mr. Conway reported on the work of the Subcommittee in the chairperson’s absence. He informed the 
Committee that all documents provided to the Subcommittee has been distributed to the full 
Committee. Mr. Conway stated that Committee members had already received a copy of the 
Superintendent’s summative report. Superintendent Skinner has also submitted supporting 
documentation outlining the goals he and his administrative team have achieved over the past two 
years. Committee members have received all evaluation materials and are expected to return their 
completed evaluation documents to Dr. Hall by September 28, 2026. Dr. Hall will compile the scores and 
comments into a master document, which will be presented to the full Committee at the School 
Committee meeting on October 7, 2026. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the report as a report of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. 
Bahou. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8 REPORTS OF THE SUPERINTENDENT 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to bundle agenda items 8.1 and 8.4; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).

8.1. Career Technical Education: 6 Programs Approved for Lowell High School 
 
Superintendent Skinner provided a report to the Committee regarding the recent confirmation from the 
Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) that six Lowell High School programs have 
been granted Career Technical Education (CTE) status. These programs include Culinary Arts, 
Information Support Services & Networking, Multimedia and Broadcast Production, Robotics & 
Automation Engineering Technology, Business Technology, and Engineering Technology. Superintendent 
Skinner noted that this designation represents a major success for the school district and is the 
culmination of years of planning, program development, and coordination with DESE’s Office for 
College, Career, and Technical Education. The designation broadens the appeal of Lowell High School to 
students seeking to develop valuable technical and employability skills, earn industry-recognized 
credentials, and explore career opportunities while still in high school. These CTE programs will provide 
meaningful pathways to college, apprenticeships, and the workforce, while helping students recognize 
the relevance and purpose of their learning. Lowell High School’s CTE students will graduate not only 
prepared for further education, but also equipped with the knowledge, skills, confidence, and 
experience needed to contribute meaningfully to the community and to a changing economy. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8.2. Response to Motion (By Dominik Lay, 05/20/2026) Regarding Middle School Financial Literacy 
 
Dr. Fox Roye, Assistant Superintendent of Academics and Instruction, informed the Committee that 
Lowell Public Schools (LPS) has a strong existing foundation for developing financial literacy among 
students in Grades 5-8 through its high-quality instructional materials (HQIM), supplemental programs, 
and alignment with the Massachusetts Curriculum Frameworks. LPS currently utilizes Eureka Math² for 
Mathematics, the Democratic Knowledge Project (DKP) for Social Studies, and OpenSciEd for Science. 
Collectively, these instructional materials provide meaningful opportunities for students to develop the 
knowledge, skills, and reasoning necessary for financial literacy. Eureka Math² provides the strongest 
and most direct connection, with financial concepts embedded across Grades 5-8, including saving, 
earning, income, rates, ratios, percentages, investments, financial modeling, and comparing costs. DKP 
Social Studies provides indirect to moderate connections through topics such as taxes, economic 
inequality, public resources, public policy, and civic and economic decision-making. OpenSciEd also 
offers opportunities to develop financial literacy-related skills through the exploration of costs, 
resources, constraints, trade-offs, efficiency, and cost-benefit analysis. Dr. Fox Roye emphasized that the 
existing progression within Eureka Math², in particular, provides a strong foundation upon which LPS can 
build a more intentional and cohesive approach to financial literacy across Grades 5-8. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin).

8.3. Enhanced Safety Recommendations 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to send agenda items 8.3. Enhanced Safety Recommendations to an Executive 
Session due to the confidential nature of the report; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion 
passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8.4. Financial Literacy Update 
 
Dr. Fox Roye, Assistant Superintendent of Academics and Instruction, informed the Committee that, in 
response to the School Committee’s recommendation to expand extended learning opportunities for 
students, the Lowell Public Schools Special Programs Department has strengthened its financial literacy 
programming through the district’s Explore & Expand initiative. This year, Lowell Public Schools was 
awarded a $6,900 Financial Education Innovation Fund Grant through the Massachusetts State 
Treasurer’s Office of Economic Empowerment to support financial literacy programming for Lowell High 
School Career Academy students. Through partnerships with Community Teamwork and Project LEARN, 
students participate in hands-on learning experiences designed to build practical financial knowledge 
and prepare them for postsecondary education, careers, and adult life. At the Community Teamwork 
Financial Education Center, students engage in two interactive financial education sessions focused on 
budgeting, banking, credit, income management, and financial decision-making, including a real-world 
budgeting simulation. Students also explore workforce readiness and entrepreneurship, helping them 
connect financial literacy skills to future career pathways. In partnership with Project LEARN, Career 
Academy students participate in career development workshops addressing career exploration, 
personality and career alignment, and time and stress management, further supporting their 
preparation for successful transitions to college, careers, and independent adulthood. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8.5. Report on Motions 
 
Superintendent Skinner provided the Committee with an updated report on the status of outstanding 
motions and asked the Committee if they had any concerns or questions. 
 
Ms. McFadden stated that M210 is not complete and would like it to remain open. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin).

8.6. Home Education 
 
Superintendent Skinner recommended that the following parents/guardians be allowed to home 
educate their child:  
Shaylee Araujo 
Clarivel Marin De Dragas 
Joyce Cedeno 
Victoria Lee 
Ariadne Oliveria

8.7. Superintendent Evaluation: Discussion of Process and Timeline 
 
This was discussed during the HR & Operations Subcommittee report. Mayor Gitschier asked the 
Committee if there were any questions or concerns regarding the proposed timeline. All Committee 
members indicated that they were comfortable with the timeline. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.7 (excluding 
8.6) as reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Mr. Bahou). 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
 
9.1. Approval to Accept and Expend Allocated FY27 Awards 
 
These grant funds have been secured by the Lowell Public Schools through the Massachusetts 
Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. 
 
Mr. Bahou to approve, accept and expend the allocated FY27 awards; the motion was seconded by 
Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
9.2. Letter of Approval for Accepting Donation to Daley School 
 
The Lowell Public Schools periodically receives monetary donations from individuals, community 
organizations, and businesses intended to support student programs, activities, and school-based 
initiatives. Donation details are as follows:  
 
➢ Ten Thousand dollars ($10,000.00) to cover the cost of 8th grade yearbooks, school culture   t-
shirts for all students, student attendance recognitions, and student social competency 
recognitions.  
➢ Five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) for supplies associated with after school activities.  
➢ Five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) for the benefit of the 7th grade team. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept the donation for the Daley School in the amount of $20,000; the motion 
was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).
(Page 6 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
9.3. Budget Modification Request 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve the budget modification in the amount of $10,000; the motion was 
seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
9.4. MOA - Continuous Rate of Pay for Paraprofessionals Serving as Substitute Teacher 
 
Dr. Hall presented an MOA to the Committee that would continue the existing rate of pay for 
paraprofessionals serving as substitute teachers. This rate of pay has been in effect since 2022. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to approve the MOA for the continuous rate of pay for paraprofessionals serving 
as a substitute teacher; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent 
(Ms. Martin). 
 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to adjourn at 7:15 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion 
passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Liam Skinner, Superintendent and 
Secretary to the Lowell School Committee
